metadata.description: License-safe synthetic scenarios inspired by public examples, tutorials, docs, bug reports, and developer war stories for comparing IntentDiff with SemanticDiff.
metadata.fixture_policy: Source URLs describe the shape of the change only. Old/new fixtures are fictional and intentionally not copied from the source.

weaknesses_to_exploit.weakness: SemanticDiff has a narrower parser matrix.
weaknesses_to_exploit.opportunity: Keep advertising broad parser coverage and enforce it with runtime language smoke tests.

weaknesses_to_exploit.weakness: SemanticDiff documents syntactically invalid code as a hard limitation for semantic diffs.
weaknesses_to_exploit.opportunity: Make IntentDiff's fallback, parse warning, and partial-parse behavior explicit and testable.

weaknesses_to_exploit.weakness: SemanticDiff is primarily a black-box visual reviewer.
weaknesses_to_exploit.opportunity: Expose structured JSON, diagnostics, review tree state, and CI-friendly reports.

weaknesses_to_exploit.weakness: SemanticDiff does not expose an obvious cross-file semantic review surface in VS Code.
weaknesses_to_exploit.opportunity: Strengthen repository-level Semantic Changes, cross-file grouping, and dependency-aware review.

weaknesses_to_exploit.weakness: SemanticDiff documents anonymous usage telemetry controlled by VS Code telemetry settings.
weaknesses_to_exploit.opportunity: Document local processing and no-telemetry behavior if true, or add an explicit privacy setting.

weaknesses_to_exploit.weakness: SemanticDiff exposes few automation surfaces beyond the editor UI.
weaknesses_to_exploit.opportunity: Add stable commands, test-only APIs, and report export for CI and review bots.

command_parity.reason: Switch an existing VS Code diff into a dedicated IntentDiff viewer.
Offer an alternate switch command for keybindings and menus.
Return from the custom semantic viewer to the stock VS Code diff.
Recompute or filter comment-only changes from the semantic viewer.
Navigate to the previous semantic change in viewer or tree context.
Navigate to the next semantic change in viewer or tree context.
The tree can open entries, but the custom viewer should expose a direct command.
Semantic Changes refresh exists; a dedicated viewer recompute command is still needed.
Changed-only custom viewer needs collapsible context.
Changed-only custom viewer needs expandable local and parent-scope context.
Offer default viewer integration once the custom viewer exists.
A stable export command can beat print-only state by producing machine-readable review artifacts.
Clear viewer caches, loaded context, and comparison mode state.

setting_parity.reason: Let users make the IntentDiff viewer the default for supported languages.
Control whether switching to the custom viewer closes the original diff tab.
Expose fallback behavior explicitly, including parse-warning and partial-parse choices.
Custom viewer should offer none/simple/detailed overview modes.
Default comment filtering behavior should be configurable.
Moved-code visualization needs an opt-in default.

separate_viewer_backlog.summary: Add a webview-based semantic diff viewer while keeping live overlays and the Semantic Changes tree.

prioritized_backlog.summary: Keep the runtime supported-language smoke matrix and discrepancy baseline current.
Build the separate changed-only IntentDiff viewer for SemanticDiff UX parity.
Add commands and settings listed in the parity matrices.
Turn Databricks, ADF, HCL, SQL, YAML, and config scenarios into high-signal tests and demos.
Improve and document partial-parse and fallback behavior on syntactically invalid edits.
Document local/no-telemetry behavior if true, or add an explicit privacy setting.

source.license_note: Inspired by Vue single-file component organization; fixture is synthetic.

scenarios.scenario_shape: Inline template handler becomes a named script function with a class addition.

fixture.old:
<template>
  <button @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue"
const count = ref(0)
</script>
fixture.new:
<template>
  <button class="counter" @click="increment">{{ count }}</button>
</template>

<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue"
const count = ref(0)

function increment() {
  count.value += 1
}
</script>

source.license_note: Inspired by Databricks task dependency and run-if configuration; fixture is synthetic.

scenarios.scenario_shape: Single-task workflow grows into a DAG with a parameter and conditional downstream task.

fixture.old:
name: revenue_daily
tasks:
  - task_key: ingest
    notebook_task:
      notebook_path: /Repos/acme/ingest
fixture.new:
name: revenue_daily
parameters:
  - name: env
    default: prod
tasks:
  - task_key: ingest
    notebook_task:
      notebook_path: /Repos/acme/ingest
  - task_key: publish
    depends_on:
      - task_key: ingest
    run_if: ALL_SUCCESS
    notebook_task:
      notebook_path: /Repos/acme/publish

source.license_note: Inspired by CTE-based query refactoring; fixture is synthetic.

scenarios.scenario_shape: Flat aggregation becomes a CTE with a windowed rank filter.

fixture.old:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM invoices
WHERE status = 'paid'
GROUP BY customer_id;
fixture.new:
WITH ranked_customers AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    SUM(amount) AS total_amount,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC) AS revenue_rank
  FROM invoices
  WHERE status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT customer_id, total_amount
FROM ranked_customers
WHERE revenue_rank <= 10;
